items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We did India. We did Richie’s Elm. They arranged three different cats to play launeddas to play the chords.

ctx.x: It’s three pipes. One is the drone. One is a fourth and fifth with this finger. And one is – I guess four notes. So it’s a triple – what do you call it? – circular breathing. 3,000 years old. They have absolute proof it was 3,000 years old. I’m always interested in where I go, bah bah boom. Could I meet the guy? I meet the master, the last living master. Name is Baranka, old cat, chain-smoking cigarettes, little Italian, 75 years old, playing the shit out of this thing. So the record date, it was arranged to meet…
meets launeddas. We did India. We did Richie’s Elm. They arranged three different cats to play launeddas to play the chords. That’s a kind of interesting record, folky type thing, ethnic.
